blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

Read the passage and answer Questions 1–13.

Mystery Drawing

Is the drawing of a young Milanese girl really by famous artist Leonardo da Vinci?

On January 30, 1998, an art auction was held in New York city. One drawing was of a pretty girl, but it attracted little attention. The catalogue listed the work as a German drawing done in ink and with coloured chalk, dating back to the early 19th century, with styling borrowed from the much earlier Renaissance period. A New York dealer, Kate Ganz, purchased the picture for $21,850. The price had barely changed almost ten years later when a Canadian collector, Peter Silverman, bought it. The drawing might actually date from the Renaissance, he thought. Ganz herself had mentioned Leonardo da Vinci as an influence on the artist. Silverman wondered whether it was the work of the great Leonardo himself, but discovery of a Da Vinci is truly rare. At the time of Silverman’s purchase, it had been more than 75 years since the last authentication of one of the artist’s paintings. It had never been recorded that Da Vinci ever made a major work like this, and neither were there any known copies. If this image was an authentic Leonardo, where had it been hiding for 500 years?

Silverman emailed a digital image of the drawing to Martin Kemp, professor of art history at Oxford University and renowned Leonardo scholar. Kemp immediately flew to Zurich, where Silverman kept the drawing in a bank vault. Kemp was excited and began his own investigation. He was aided by Pascal Cotte of Lumière Technology in Paris, who used high resolution multispectral scans which allowed Kemp to study the drawing’s different layers. The more Kemp looked, the more he saw what he considered evidence of Leonardo’s hand: the beautiful tone of the colours, the precise lines, and the fact that the shaded areas showed distinctive strokes just like Leonardo’s. The subject’s expression was self-confident but thoughtful. She appeared to be someone growing up too fast, and conveyed Leonardo’s belief that a portrait should reveal ‘motion of the mind’.

Kemp also needed proof that the portrait had been made during Leonardo's lifetime (1452-1519) and that its historical details fitted the artist's biography. Material analysis strongly suggested that the artist had used calfskin, quite normal for the time, and this was then carbon-dated. Its origin was placed somewhere between 1440 and 1650. Then costume research revealed that the girl belonged specifically to the Milanese court of the 1490s, with its fashion for elaborately bound hair. Leonardo lived in Milan during this time, accepting commissions for portraits of people in the royal court. Stitch marks on the edge of the portrait suggested that it came from a book, possibly the sort, common at the time, that would commemorate a royal marriage.

Kemp's detective work led him to a name, Bianca Sforza. A daughter of the Duke of Milan, she was married in 1496 to Galeazzo Sanseverino, commander of the Milanese troops and a patron of Leonardo's. Tragically, she died a few months later. In 2010 Kemp and Cotte published their findings in a book. Several prominent Leonardo scholars agreed, others were sceptical. The possibility of a high-quality forgery was raised. Doubt centred around the drawing’s sudden, almost miraculous appearance. Where had it come from?

Kemp didn’t know. Then, quite unexpectedly, a message came from David Wright, professor of art history at the University of South Florida. Having followed the very public dispute, Wright suggested to Kemp, whom he had never met, that his answer might lie in the National Library of Poland in Warsaw, inside a book called the Sforziad. Wright, an expert on Renaissance iconography, described it as a commemorative volume for the marriage of Bianca Sforza, a suitable occasion for a Leonardo portrait.

Kemp and Cotte travelled to Warsaw. Cotte’s macrophotography revealed that a page had been removed from the exact place in the Sforziad where a portrait would have been added. The moment arrived when they inserted a copy of Bianca’s portrait into the open book. It fitted perfectly. For Kemp, this was the proof. It was a single portrait by Leonardo that had gone into a book and then onto a shelf.

According to Wright, the volume reached Poland in the early 1500s, when a member of the Sforza family married a Polish royal. The page was removed, possibly at the time of the book’s rebinding in the 17th or 18th century. The trail grows faint here. What is known is that at some point it was acquired by an Italian man, a specialist in art restoration, and that his widow put it up for sale at auction.

These are amazing times for Leonardo admirers. Recently, London’s National Gallery exhibited Leonardo’s painting of Jesus Christ holding a globe, a work lost for centuries. In Florence, researchers looking for Leonardo’s Battle of Anghiari, last seen in the mid-1500s, are using technology to find out if the painting might be hidden behind a wall in the Palazzo Vecchio, but the issue has not yet been resolved.

Authenticating a centuries-old artwork is seldom an objective process. Ego, personal taste, and fear of legal cases all contribute to the judgement. To reach wider consensus, Kemp sent his latest findings to a number of leading specialists, almost all of whom declined to comment. Agreement ‘will take time’ concedes Kemp, ‘but I have clear confidence in the research we’ve done. One thing is sure, should the day come when Bianca Sforza’s face hangs in a museum as a true Leonardo, everyone will stare.’

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 1–7

Complete the notes. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER from the text for each answer.

The drawing’s discovery and early research

Art dealer Kate Ganz bought a drawing of a girl made using chalk and ink.

Ganz sold the drawing to art collector Peter Silverman.

Silverman suspected the portrait was by Leonardo da Vinci but knew that

1 no new Da Vinci work had been found for over years

2 no of the portrait were believed to exist

Martin Kemp believed the drawing may be by Da Vinci because of

the lines and colours

3 the used in the drawing’s darker shaded areas

4 the on the girl’s face

Proof that the drawing had been done in Da Vinci’s lifetime came from

5 the age of the used as material

6 the style of the girl’s clothing and

7 the kind of the drawing had been taken from

Questions 8–13

Choose TRUE if the statement agrees with the information given in the text, choose FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or choose NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

8 In 2010, there were mixed reactions to Kemp and Cotte’s research on the drawing.

9 Kemp contacted Professor David Wright for his advice on the drawing.

10 An Italian art restorer attempted to restore the colour to the drawing.

11 Research has revealed the location of Da Vinci’s painting Battle of Anghiari.

12 There has been a refusal by most Da Vinci experts to respond to Kemp’s findings.

13 Kemp now doubts whether the drawing was really done by Da Vinci.

items.text:
题目翻译：Silverman 怀疑这幅肖像出自 Leonardo da Vinci 之手，但他知道：已有超过______年没有发现新的 Da Vinci 作品。
答案：75
解析：原文说，Silverman 买画时，距上一次鉴定出这位画家的真迹已超过75年。题干 over 对应 more than，且 years 已给出，所以只填 75。末尾的500年说的是画作可能隐匿的时长，不是两次发现之间的间隔。
定位：正文第1段
At the time of Silverman’s purchase, it had been more than 75 years since the last authentication of one of the artist’s paintings.
原文翻译：Silverman 购买这幅画时，距上一次有画作被鉴定为这位艺术家的真迹，已经过去了超过75年。

题目翻译：Silverman 怀疑这幅肖像出自 Leonardo da Vinci 之手，但他知道：人们认为，这幅肖像不存在任何______。
答案：copies
解析：题干 no ... were believed to exist 对应原文 neither were there any known copies，即也没有已知摹本。因此填 copies，保留原文复数；题干中的 were 也与复数一致。
定位：正文第1段
It had never been recorded that Da Vinci ever made a major work like this, and neither were there any known copies.
原文翻译：从未有记录表明 Da Vinci 创作过这样一幅重要作品，也没有任何已知的摹本。

题目翻译：Martin Kemp 认为这幅画可能出自 Da Vinci 之手，依据之一是：画中较暗的阴影区域所用的______。
答案：strokes
解析：darker shaded areas 锁定原文 shaded areas showed distinctive strokes，指暗部独特的笔触，因此填 strokes。线条和色彩已列在题目上一个项目中，本空问的是阴影区域所用的笔触。
定位：正文第2段
The more Kemp looked, the more he saw what he considered evidence of Leonardo’s hand: the beautiful tone of the colours, the precise lines, and the fact that the shaded areas showed distinctive strokes just like Leonardo’s.
原文翻译：Kemp 看得越仔细，就越能发现一些被他视为画作出自 Leonardo 之手的迹象：优美的色调、精确的线条，以及阴影区域中与 Leonardo 的笔法如出一辙的独特笔触。

题目翻译：Martin Kemp 认为这幅画可能出自 Da Vinci 之手，依据之一是：女孩脸上的______。
答案：expression
解析：原文直接描述画中人物的 expression，既自信又若有所思，正对应女孩脸上的特征，因此填 expression。后面的 motion of the mind 说明肖像创作理念，并不是本空所问的面部特征。
定位：正文第2段
The subject’s expression was self-confident but thoughtful.
原文翻译：画中人物的神情自信，却又若有所思。

题目翻译：证明这幅画创作于 Da Vinci 在世期间的证据之一，是：用作画材的______的年代。
答案：calfskin
解析：题干把“材料的年代”列为证据。原文先指出画家使用 calfskin，随后说明对这种材料进行了碳测年，所以填 calfskin。1440—1650是测年范围，本空问的是材料名称。
定位：正文第3段
Material analysis strongly suggested that the artist had used calfskin, quite normal for the time, and this was then carbon-dated. Its origin was placed somewhere between 1440 and 1650.
原文翻译：材料分析强烈表明，画家使用了小牛皮，这在当时相当常见；随后，研究人员对它进行了碳测年。测年结果将它的年代范围确定在1440年至1650年之间。

题目翻译：证明这幅画创作于 Da Vinci 在世期间的证据之一，是：女孩的服饰和______的样式。
答案：hair
解析：服饰研究把女孩与1490年代的米兰宫廷联系起来，并特别提到当地精心束发的风尚，对应题干 clothing and hair，填 hair。court 是所属宫廷，不是与服饰并列的外观特征。
定位：正文第3段
Then costume research revealed that the girl belonged specifically to the Milanese court of the 1490s, with its fashion for elaborately bound hair.
原文翻译：接着，服饰研究表明，画中女孩正是1490年代的米兰宫廷中人，当时流行精心束起的发型。

题目翻译：证明这幅画创作于 Da Vinci 在世期间的证据之一，是：这幅画原先所在的______的种类。
答案：book
解析：肖像边缘的缝线痕迹表明，它原本来自一本书，可能是一类纪念王室婚礼的书。因此 kind of 后填 book。后文的 Sforziad 是具体书名，本空要求的是载体类别。
定位：正文第3段
Stitch marks on the edge of the portrait suggested that it came from a book, possibly the sort, common at the time, that would commemorate a royal marriage.
原文翻译：肖像边缘的缝线痕迹表明，它原本来自一本书，可能是当时常见的那种纪念王室婚礼的书。

items.text:
题目翻译：2010年，人们对 Kemp 和 Cotte 关于这幅画的研究反应不一。
答案：TRUE
解析：Kemp 和 Cotte 在2010年出版研究结果；紧接着原文说，几位著名学者赞同，另一些人怀疑。赞同与怀疑并存就是 mixed reactions（反应不一），与题干一致，因此为 TRUE。
定位：正文第4段
In 2010 Kemp and Cotte published their findings in a book. Several prominent Leonardo scholars agreed, others were sceptical.
原文翻译：2010年，Kemp 和 Cotte 将研究结果结集出版。几位著名的 Leonardo 研究学者表示赞同，另一些人则持怀疑态度。

题目翻译：Kemp 联系了 David Wright 教授，就这幅画向他征求意见。
答案：FALSE
解析：原文说消息意外地从 David Wright 那里传来，随后是 Wright 向从未见过面的 Kemp 提出建议。题干却把联系方向改成 Kemp 主动向 Wright 求教，与原文相反，因此为 FALSE。
定位：正文第5段
Then, quite unexpectedly, a message came from David Wright, professor of art history at the University of South Florida. Having followed the very public dispute, Wright suggested to Kemp, whom he had never met, that his answer might lie in the National Library of Poland in Warsaw, inside a book called the Sforziad.
原文翻译：这时，南佛罗里达大学（University of South Florida）的艺术史教授 David Wright 意外地发来了一条消息。Wright 一直关注着这场公开争论；他向素未谋面的 Kemp 提出，答案也许藏在华沙（Warsaw）的波兰国家图书馆（National Library of Poland）里，藏在一本名为《Sforziad》的书中。

题目翻译：一位意大利艺术品修复师曾尝试恢复这幅画的颜色。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：原文只说一位意大利艺术品修复专家曾获得这幅画，以及他的遗孀后来将画作送去拍卖。职业是修复师，并不能证明他实际修复过这幅画的颜色；文中也没有否认他做过，所以为 NOT GIVEN。
定位：正文第7段
What is known is that at some point it was acquired by an Italian man, a specialist in art restoration, and that his widow put it up for sale at auction.
原文翻译：已知的是，这幅画后来曾由一位意大利男子获得；他是一位艺术品修复专家，他的遗孀将画作送上了拍卖会。

题目翻译：研究已经揭示了 Da Vinci 画作《Battle of Anghiari》的位置。
答案：FALSE
解析：研究人员正在调查画作是否藏在 Palazzo Vecchio 的墙后，且作者明确说 the issue has not yet been resolved（问题尚未解决）。这与题干 has revealed 所说的“已经查明位置”相反，因此为 FALSE。文中有明确的未解决状态，不能选 NOT GIVEN。
定位：正文第8段
In Florence, researchers looking for Leonardo’s Battle of Anghiari, last seen in the mid-1500s, are using technology to find out if the painting might be hidden behind a wall in the Palazzo Vecchio, but the issue has not yet been resolved.
原文翻译：在佛罗伦萨（Florence），研究人员正借助技术寻找 Leonardo 的《Battle of Anghiari》；这幅画最后一次被人看见是在16世纪中叶，他们想查明它是否藏在旧宫（Palazzo Vecchio）的一堵墙后，但这个问题至今尚未解决。

题目翻译：大多数 Da Vinci 专家拒绝回应 Kemp 的研究发现。
答案：TRUE
解析：Kemp 将发现寄给一批顶尖专家，其中 almost all（几乎所有人）declined to comment（拒绝置评）。这支持题干 most experts refused to respond，故为 TRUE。拒绝评论不等于已经判定画作是假画。
定位：正文第9段
To reach wider consensus, Kemp sent his latest findings to a number of leading specialists, almost all of whom declined to comment.
原文翻译：为争取更广泛的共识，Kemp 将最新发现寄给了一批顶尖专家，但其中几乎所有人都拒绝置评。

题目翻译：Kemp 现在怀疑这幅画是否真是 Da Vinci 所作。
答案：FALSE
解析：Kemp 说同行达成共识还需要时间，但他自己明确表示 I have clear confidence in the research we’ve done。等待共识不等于他对自己的结论产生怀疑，因此题干与其态度相反，选 FALSE。
定位：正文第9段
Agreement ‘will take time’ concedes Kemp, ‘but I have clear confidence in the research we’ve done.
原文翻译：Kemp 承认，达成共识“还需要时间”，但他说：“我对我们所做的研究有充分的信心。”

题目翻译：研究已经揭示了 Da Vinci 画作《Battle of Anghiari》的位置。
答案：FALSE
解析：研究人员正在调查画作是否藏在 Palazzo Vecchio 的墙后，且作者明确说 the issue has not yet been resolved（问题尚未解决）。这与题干 has revealed 所说的“已经查明位置”相反，因此为 FALSE。文中有明确的未解决状态，不能选 NOT GIVEN。
定位：正文第8段
In Florence, researchers looking for Leonardo’s Battle of Anghiari, last seen in the mid-1500s, are using technology to find out if the painting might be hidden behind a wall in the Palazzo Vecchio, but the issue has not yet been resolved.
原文翻译：在佛罗伦萨（Florence），研究人员正借助技术寻找 Leonardo 的《Battle of Anghiari》；这幅画最后一次被人看见是在16世纪中叶，他们想查明它是否藏在旧宫（Palazzo Vecchio）的一堵墙后，但这个问题至今尚未解决。

题目翻译：大多数 Da Vinci 专家拒绝回应 Kemp 的研究发现。
答案：TRUE
解析：Kemp 将发现寄给一批顶尖专家，其中 almost all（几乎所有人）declined to comment（拒绝置评）。这支持题干 most experts refused to respond，故为 TRUE。拒绝评论不等于已经判定画作是假画。
定位：正文第9段
To reach wider consensus, Kemp sent his latest findings to a number of leading specialists, almost all of whom declined to comment.
原文翻译：为争取更广泛的共识，Kemp 将最新发现寄给了一批顶尖专家，但其中几乎所有人都拒绝置评。

题目翻译：Kemp 现在怀疑这幅画是否真是 Da Vinci 所作。
答案：FALSE
解析：Kemp 说同行达成共识还需要时间，但他自己明确表示 I have clear confidence in the research we’ve done。等待共识不等于他对自己的结论产生怀疑，因此题干与其态度相反，选 FALSE。
定位：正文第9段
Agreement ‘will take time’ concedes Kemp, ‘but I have clear confidence in the research we’ve done.
原文翻译：Kemp 承认，达成共识“还需要时间”，但他说：“我对我们所做的研究有充分的信心。”
